title: the night the moon bled
body:
Writing
Prologue: The Night the Moon Bled
For a thousand years, the moon watched over the world of Elarion.
Its silver light protected humanity from the creatures hiding beyond the veil of darkness. Ancient legends called it the Last Moon—the final seal holding an ancient evil beneath the earth.
But one night, the moon turned crimson.
Across the kingdom, every clock stopped at midnight. The stars vanished. Rivers turned black, and shadows began moving without their owners.
From the ruins of forgotten temples came a whisper:
“The seal is broken. The forgotten king will return.”
In a small village at the edge of the world, a seventeen-year-old boy named Kael awakened with a strange symbol glowing on his wrist. He had seen that symbol only once before—in the final letter left by his missing mother.
The letter contained just one warning:
“When the moon bleeds, trust no one—not even the light.”
That same night, creatures of darkness attacked his village. As flames swallowed the streets, Kael discovered something impossible: the shadows obeyed his voice.
A mysterious girl named Lyra, carrying a broken silver blade, rescued him and revealed the truth.
Kael was not an ordinary human.
He was the last descendant of the Eclipse Guardians, an order believed to have vanished centuries ago. Their blood carried the power to control the boundary between light and darkness.
And now that power was awakening.
Chapter One: The Boy Beneath the Crimson Sky
Kael and Lyra journey toward the ruined capital of Veyra, searching for answers about his mother and the red moon.
Along the way, they encounter abandoned cities, cursed forests, and survivors who have begun worshipping the darkness. Kael struggles to control his growing abilities, discovering that every time he uses his power, he loses a fragment of a memory.
Meanwhile, a masked figure known as the Hollow King commands the creatures spreading across the kingdom. He seems to know Kael personally—and calls him the key to the world's destruction.
Chapter Two: The Gate Beneath the Sea
Their search leads them to an ancient gate hidden beneath a drowned temple. According to Lyra, the gate contains one of the seven Eclipse Relics, artifacts capable of restoring the moon's seal.
But the temple is alive.
Its walls whisper secrets. Its corridors change when no one is watching. And a mysterious relic reacts to Kael as if it has been waiting for him for centuries.
When Kael touches it, he sees a vision of his mother standing beside the Hollow King.
Before he can understand what he has witnessed, the gate opens—and something on the other side speaks his true name.
Chapter Three: The City Without Shadows
The heroes arrive in Noctis, a city where no shadows exist and nobody remembers the last sunrise.
There, they meet an underground resistance fighting the Hollow King's followers. Kael learns that the crimson eclipse is not merely a celestial event. It is a countdown.
With every passing night, the barrier between worlds weakens.
Yet the resistance hides a dangerous secret: someone among them has been secretly delivering Eclipse Relics to the enemy.
Trust begins to fracture, and Lyra's past becomes as mysterious as Kael's own.
Chapter Four: The Seven Relics
Kael discovers that seven ancient relics were created to maintain the balance between light and darkness. Gathering them may restore the seal—but each relic tests a different part of its bearer.
One demands courage. Another demands truth. A third demands sacrifice—not of life, but of the memories that define who a person is.
As Kael grows stronger, he begins forgetting the faces, voices, and moments that once gave his life meaning.
He must decide how much of himself he is willing to lose to save a world that may fear him more than the monsters attacking it.
Chapter Five: The Truth Behind the Eclipse
The greatest revelation comes when Kael discovers that the Hollow King was once an Eclipse Guardian.
Long ago, the Guardians attempted to destroy darkness completely. Their experiment shattered the balance between the worlds and imprisoned an entire civilization beyond the veil.
The Hollow King seeks revenge, believing that the only way to restore his people is to extinguish the moon and merge both worlds.
Kael's mother helped seal the breach—and disappeared while trying to find another solution.
Now Kael faces a truth that changes everything: the darkness is not entirely evil, and the light is not entirely innocent.
The real enemy is the broken balance between them.
Final Arc: The Last Moon
As the final eclipse approaches, kingdoms fall and ancient powers awaken. Kael and Lyra race toward the Moonspire, where the original seal was created.
The Hollow King offers Kael a choice: restore the old world by repeating the Guardians' mistake, or destroy the seal and risk allowing both worlds to collide.
But Kael discovers a forgotten third possibility.
The Last Moon was never meant to imprison darkness forever. It was meant to unite two worlds that had forgotten how to coexist.
In the final battle beneath a crimson sky, Kael must master both sides of his power—not by conquering one with the other, but by accepting them both.
The moon begins to shine silver once more.
Yet as peace returns, a final message appears on the broken relic:
“The first eclipse was only the beginning.”
Far beyond the restored moon, another light awakens in the endless darkness.
And someone, somewhere, begins to laugh.
